source.title: The Effect of Model Size on Worst-Group Generalization
source.authors: Alan Pham; Eunice Chan; V. Srivatsa; Dhruba Ghosh; Yaoqing Yang; Yao-Dong Yu; Ruiqi Zhong; Joseph E. Gonzalez; Jacob Steinhardt

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps model size and reports test-error outcomes, but focuses on worst-group error under ERM rather than the usual overall test-error curve and does not locate an interpolation threshold.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the study's stated worst-group test-error trends across size sweeps. Average test error is plotted, but the text does not describe its size trend and the supplied figure extraction does not provide readable values. The group-DRO comparison in Table 3 is cited prior work, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures worst-group test error against model size under ERM, a related but different construct from the overall test error that V1 and V4 name. It never locates an interpolation threshold or reports a fall-rise-fall in test error. Double descent appears only in related work as background. Average test error is plotted but never described in the text.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that under ERM larger models generally do not hurt, and sometimes help, worst-group test accuracy across nearly all settings. Growing pre-trained models is more likely to help than growing from-scratch ones, with consistent gains on Waterbirds and MultiNLI. They advise using larger pre-trained models when group labels are unknown, and group DRO when they are known.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies depth and width across vision and language model families and evaluates worst-group test error under ERM. It does not reproduce the original double-descent setup or measure error around an interpolation threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trend differs by initialization and dataset: pre-trained models improve on Waterbirds and MultiNLI, while CelebA results are roughly unchanged; scratch-trained models generally do not improve.

fits_no_version.finding: Under ERM, worst-group test error falls or stays flat with model size (depth and width). It falls for pre-trained models on Waterbirds and MultiNLI, is roughly flat on CelebA, and is roughly flat for from-scratch models. No intermediate rise is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing model size does not hurt worst-group (rare-subgroup) test error under ERM with spurious correlations, and helps for pre-trained models.

fits_no_version.finding: In setups copied from Nakkiran et al. (ResNet10 width on CelebA) and Mei & Montanari (random features on Waterbirds), worst-group error decreases then saturates. On Waterbirds it stays around 50% above 10^3 features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In double-descent-style width and feature sweeps, worst-group error shows no reported peak and saturates at high width.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on Distribution Shifts, 35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021)
record.problems: The main reported conclusions concern worst-group rather than average test error. The paper does not locate the interpolation threshold or report the tested curve shape over epochs or sample size. Trends are mostly described qualitatively; exact values are not given in the text for most model-size comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Average train and average test errors appear in Figures 1–7, but the text does not state their size trends and the supplied figure extraction does not provide readable plotted values to assign. No other directly relevant result was excluded.

missing.what: Average test error vs width or number of features in the Nakkiran-style ResNet10 CelebA sweep and the Mei–Montanari random-features Waterbirds sweep. These are double-descent setups; curves are plotted but the text gives no values or trend description.
Average test error vs depth and width for pre-trained and from-scratch ResNet, VGG BN, MobileNet and BERT. Plotted, but the text gives no values or trend.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges V1' label is withdrawn. The study's measure is worst-group error, it never locates the interpolation threshold, and the models span only overparameterized pre-trained families. Absence of a worst-group peak therefore cannot challenge model-wise double descent in test error. The Figure 7 sweeps replicate double-descent setups and could bear on V1 and V4 if the average-test-error curves were readable. The Table 3 DRO numbers are cited from Sagawa et al. and should not become rows.

versions.untested_parts: Tests model-size trends in worst-group test error under ERM. Does not establish a peak near the size that just fits the training set, or test the full fall-rise-fall shape in ordinary average test error.

rows.subject: Pre-trained model series (ResNet, VGG BN, MobileNet, and BERT; aggregate results)
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size and evaluated worst-group test error after ERM training to convergence.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval error bars are included in graphs; values not stated
rows.note: The study describes decreasing worst-group error with increasing pre-trained model size on Waterbirds; the result is reported across the relevant model-size series.
rows.check: Measure is worst-group test error, not overall test error, so it does not bear on V1. Calling a decreasing trend 'absent' was a misreading. Move to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: BERT (pre-trained; aggregate depth- and width-varying results)
rows.operation_detail: Varied BERT depth and width and evaluated worst-group test error after ERM training to convergence.
rows.value: monotonically improves in accuracy as model size increases
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval error bars are included in graphs; values not stated
rows.note: The text reports monotonic improvement in worst-group accuracy for larger pre-trained models on MultiNLI.
rows.check: Worst-group error on MultiNLI with BERT is a different construct from overall test error. Move to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Pre-trained model series (ResNet and VGG BN; aggregate results)
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size and evaluated worst-group test error after ERM training to convergence.
rows.value: increasing model size neither significantly increases nor decreases worst-group test error
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval error bars are included in graphs; values not stated
rows.note: Reported as a negligible or non-significant size effect.
rows.check: Worst-group error, not overall test error. The flat trend says nothing about a peak at the interpolation threshold, which is not located.

rows.subject: Randomly initialized model series (ResNet, VGG BN, MobileNet, and BERT; aggregate results)
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size and evaluated worst-group test error after ERM training to convergence.

conditions.value: Waterbirds, CelebA Blond / Male, CelebA Lipstick / Earring, and MultiNLI

rows.value: model size does not hurt worst-group test error; unlike pre-trained models, error did not improve with increasing size
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval error bars are included in graphs; values not stated
rows.note: Aggregate statement about the randomly initialized experiments; model-family and dataset-specific curves are shown in the cited figures.
rows.check: Worst-group error aggregated across from-scratch models. It is a different measure, and the row pools several datasets and architectures.

rows.subject: Pre-trained ResNet18 and ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Compared the worst-group test error at the two stated ResNet depths.
rows.value: pre-trained ResNet152 decreases worst-group error by approximately 18.39%
rows.note: This is a stated endpoint comparison; the text does not give values for the intermediate sizes in this specific comparison.
rows.check: This is a two-endpoint worst-group comparison (ResNet18 vs ResNet152), with no bearing on curve shape. The 18.39% figure is ambiguous between absolute and relative.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Tested ERM model-size sweeps measured by worst-group test error
reader_labels.reason: The reported sweeps show decreasing, unchanged, or otherwise non-increasing worst-group error with size, rather than the predicted intermediate rise; see r1–r5. The ResNet endpoint comparison alone does not establish curve shape (r6).
